description: In anticipation of the big track meet, Veronica struggles to find a track event she excels at, while Moose is convinced someone is making a play for Midge and all evidence points to Archie.

Jealous of the attention Betty's sand sculptures are getting, Veronica concocts a series of schemes to get the limelight back. Betty may have lost her ring in the s'mores she prepared for the gang. Vests For All Occasions fashion page with Veronica. Veronica shows up at the beach in baggy shorts and over-sized boots in her latest ploy to be the center of attention.

With the economics teacher out sick, Mr. Weatherbee installs the best student in the class as the substitute teacher. While at the mall, Veronica gets glamor photos taken of Jellybean, and of herself. Veronica moves in with the Coopers after Veronica has her credit cards rescinded.

When Betty is hospitalized for exhaustion, Veronica needs to prove that she is Betty's best friend so she volunteers as a candy striper, causing havoc at the hospital. Veronica might fail her home economics class since she has trouble cooking a gourmet meal for two for only twenty-five dollars. Betty and Veronica argue about the virtues of plastic surgery, and later, when Veronica's face is bandaged after an allergic reaction, Betty thinks she's had a procedure done.

When Veronica finds it too tedious to keep up with a written diary, she hires a film crew to produce a video diary, but that doesn't work out either. The girls want to get on the Bump 'n' Grind dance TV show, and Betty is picked, but Veronica's dancing isn't good enough. Veronica buys two wild reindeer, and they disrupt a fancy party her parents are throwing.

Archie is in danger of failing geometry without a tutor. While entertaining hospitalized children, Veronica falls asleep on a gurney in clown makeup and is mistaken for a misplaced corpse. Veronica spills Jughead's ant farm in the Lodge mansion just before she's due to host a perfume-testing party, and the ants invite themselves to the party.

Mr. Lodge signs a deal with rock artist Blondonna to endorse his cola. Svenson overhears Archie and Betty talking about the dessert she made for Home Economics class and thinks they've planted a bomb in the school. Veronica tries to lure Archie away from Cheryl with expensive gifts.

Betty tries to take Veronica hiking, but Veronica just can't leave civilization behind. Mr. Lodge doesn't share Veronica's enthusiasm for a new band called "The Dipsticks." Veronica gets a trampoline.

Cheryl plots to have Jason romance Betty and a friend named Adam romance Veronica, leaving her path to Archie free and clear. Veronica is forced to disguise herself as a frump, due to heavier than usual notoriety. Veronica sprains her ankle performing gymnastics.

For laughs, Veronica takes Betty for a spin in the virtual reality spaceship simulator at her father's aerospace lab. Veronica rids herself of three hideously garish outfits, or so she thinks. A new student at Riverdale quickly annoys everyone with his selfish, anti-social behavior.

For ruining her hair with a home perm, Veronica files suit against Betty and it's adjudicated in the school's Legal Affairs class, with Archie as presiding judge. Veronica laments that her privileged lifestyle gives her no purpose, so Betty takes her to see a wise man atop a nearby mountain.

Sugarplum, a fairy, is fired from her job at the North Pole and comes to visit the girls to find a new career. The girls are arguing and Sugarplum gets them to come back together by making them both jealous of Archie's attentions to her. Sugarplum preaches a lesson about stealing to a boy who tries to use her for a Christmas present. Santa shows up at a party and gives Sugarplum her old job back.

Betty tries to interest Veronica in rock climbing, but Veronica is resistant until she sees the type of buff guys the sport attracts. Veronica's new cellular phone is driving everyone else nuts. Veronica cuts her hair to short and curly, then immediately regrets it when nobody recognizes her.
Betty wins a contest and becomes a finalist to be the All-American Girl professional model. Mr. Lodge finds Betty and Veronica engrossed in a "current affairs" program.

Veronica agrees to finance the purchase of a 1957 classic auto in dire need of fixing up, knowing that Betty will spend all of her time fixing it, leaving Veronica a clear path at a cute new student. Veronica is taking no chances in school during the two days before her planned ski trip.

Betty innocently combines scents from scent cards in a fashion magazine and comes up with a perfume that is instantly intoxicating to anyone who smells it. Betty gets stuck in a full body alien costume. Betty agrees to help Veronica paint her room to match the color of her favorite nail polish.

Betty and Veronica receive a mysterious note promising to be a map leading to rich rewards. When Veronica learns that Betty is mentoring a pre-teen girl through the Big Sister program, she decides it would be fun to try. Betty falls asleep at the beach and dreams she and Veronica are characters out of Xena, Warrior Princess, fighting over Archie.

Jealous of the praise Betty is receiving for decorating the gym for the big dance, Veronica decides to make a grand, florid entrance in order to upstage her friend. The class is asked to bring a young person in that the particular student has had a positive influence on. To raise money for the football team, Veronica auctions off the car-washing services of both herself and Betty.

"Blame That Tune," When The Archies won't let Betty or Veronica perform solos of songs written by Brigitte, the girls quit the band and form a trio with Brigitte.

"Burnin' Up," As a class assignment, Betty and Veronica spend a day at a Riverdale Fire Station; Veronica proves to be distracted, inept and accident prone, until something close to her becomes involved.

"Caught In the Act," A reporter gets a picture of Mr. Lodge using Veronica's karaoke machine and prints it, to Mr. Lodge's dismay.

"That's of Snow Account!" Part 1 and 2, A Count visits the Lodges and steals their jewelry; Betty and Veronica come up with a plan to catch the thieves before they can skip town.

"Throw the Book at Her!"; Veronica volunteers at a library for extra credit and Betty has to train her; Not surprisingly, it's a disaster.

"Isn't That Ice?", Betty makes an ice sculpture of Archie and Veronica accidentally runs it over with her car.

"Just Desserts" Part 1 and 2, Betty and Veronica argue over whose food gift to injured Jughead is better; They decide to hang with their own kind of people: Betty with Brigitte and Veronica with Cheryl.

"Dear Betty and Veronica," Betty and Veronica become the advice columnists for the school newspaper.

"Photo Op!", Betty feels scorned by Veronica when she is not included in the innumerable pictures of Veronica's friends.

Veronica discovers a genie in an old lamp she bought and wishes for Archie to be her eternal slave. Betty and Veronica separately discover that the other has donated a gift given by them to a charity bazaar. Injured feelings ensue. As a balm for her lack of funds, Betty suggests the school dance be an "Out-Of-Style" dance, with outfits picked up at flea markets and used clothing stores.

"She's the One!", Betty tries to be more like Veronica and Veronica tries to be more like Betty.

"Plant One on Me," Cousin Fern comes to visit.

"Flower Power," When Veronica accidentally destroys Betty's flower garden she panics and transplants flowers from the nearby woods.

"Photo-Op?", Veronica picks up photos from a developer but the photos are not theirs; They show Archie and some strange person who appears to be stalking Archie so Veronica hires an investigator to find out who is stalking Archie.

"She's the One!", Betty tries to be more like Veronica and Veronica tries to be more like Betty.

"Plant One on Me," Cousin Fern comes to visit.

"Flower Power," When Veronica accidentally destroys Betty's flower garden she panics and transplants flowers from the nearby woods.

"Photo-Op?", Veronica picks up photos from a developer but the photos are not theirs.

Spurred by their competitive nature, Betty and Veronica sign on with a local women's roller derby team. The class is assigned to research their family history and Veronica finds some disturbing things in hers. Veronica's I.Q. test score gets accidentally switched with Dilton's, and quickly she's lording her I.Q. number over everyone.

"Invasion Of The Herbees" After missing them last Christmas, the gang can't wait to get their hands on some interactive Herbees! Once they get them, however, they wish they hadn't, as the needy toys demand all of their time! Be careful what you wish for, gang!

"Millennium Menagerie" Riverdale High hosts a novel theme day, the students will dress as endangered species who may not survive the next century! Will the students bring to light the animals' plight or simply prove to Mr. Weatherbee once and for all that his high school is a zoo?!

"Scents and Sensibility" Archie finds out that perfume's not the only thing that stinks when he gets the bills for Betty and Veronica's fragrant gifts!

Impressed with Betty's ability to copy his original fashions at a glance, a famous fashion designer recruits her to work with him on a new line. Jealous of all the attention Betty is getting by flying a kite in the park, Veronica teams up with Reggie to sabotage everyone's fun. A local talk show host, Ochre Wintery (Oprah Winfrey), solicits people involved in love triangles to appear on the show.

"The Love Letters": In this poignant tale, the girls pour through old mementos found in a trunk Brigitte bought at a yard sale. When they discover both love letters and sheet music from a lovesick World War II soldier to his estranged girlfriend, the girls decide to investigate. Recording the soldier's love song, Brigitte gets it played on the radio, which leads to the reunion of the star-crossed lovers. Will the reunion be bittersweet, or a brand-new beginning? Don't miss this very special story!

"Soccer- Mania": Inspired by the Women's World Cup soccer victory, the girls of Riverdale High throw themselves body and soul into the popular sport. Now the boys know how it feels to take a back seat to sports!

"Welcome To The New Millennium": Reggie says "bah, humbug!" to the new Millennium, claiming it's just another year. Until the gang proves him wrong by showing up the next day in funky, space-age outfits and demonstrating Dilton's latest scientific advances!

"Two For One": Talk about two-timing! When identical twins start dating both Betty and Veronica, they decide to pull the old switcheroo on a "double date" that's one for the books! Brigitte tips off our heroines, and soon they're plotting their own "bait and switch," with a masquerade dance providing the perfect opportunity! When the smoke clears, it's "double trouble" for the treacherous twins!

"Frankie's Back!": It's been three years since Frankie Valdez's last major appearance. Now, he and his family have returned from Puerto Rico, and he's agreed to see Maria again. But what's this? Betty and Veronica have spotted him with Brigitte! Is Frankie pulling an Archie?!

"That's Pretty Fishy": Betty and Brigitte invite Veronica to fish with them - provided her yakking doesn't scare the fish away! With her expensive, high tech equipment, you'd think she's fishing for whales!

"Look Into My Eyes": Veronica's not chicken to be on television - until a hypnotist convinces her she's a chicken on national TV!

"California, Here We Come!", Betty and Veronica hit the road for a summer trip to California!; Along the way, the girls see many historic sights and nearly turn Washington upside down, not to mention falling for the same guy!; Haven't we been down this road' before?!

"Golf Gaff," Reggie and Archie take Betty and Veronica golfing and the girls end up liking the game so much they spend all their time at the golf course.

"Starstruck"; Brigitte gets to meet her idol, Beverly Starsand (Barbra Streisand styled character), and Betty and Veronica invite themselves along.

In anticipation of this fall's Charlie's Angels: The Movie, Archie Comics gives its own spin to the popular tale of the daring female detectives, "Archie's Angels!" Betty, Veronica, and Brigitte make crime-fighting glamorous when they work undercover for the mysterious (and barely seen) Archie! Their first case: rescue the kidnapped multi-billionaire, Hiram Bigbucks (a.k.a. Mr. Lodge)! The terrific trio proves they have the brains to go with their beauty as they tackle the sinister Seymour Trump (a.k.a. Cheryl Blossom's father - you knew she'd get in on the action!). Get a jump on Angel-mania - don't miss this thrilling issue!

"Kiddie Time": Move over, Barney - the kids at Riverdale High are producing their own kiddie show, and klutzy Digby The Dodo, alias Archie (who else?) is the latest pied piper of the diaper set!

"Chores Galore": It's worse than a rejected credit card - Mr. Lodge is making Veronica do chores! Of course, she'll figure out a way to trick Betty into doing them for her. After all, what are non-rich friends for?

"Online & Out of Line": Tired of always being broke, Archie plans to impress the girls by making money auctioning off his unwanted stuff online. But when the girls find all their old presents to Archie on the auction block, Archie may be auctioning himself out of future dates!

"I Will Survive," Cast your votes?; Will Betty or Veronica be booted off the island in this riotous spoof of Survivor?!; Betty and Veronica get picked to be on the Survival Island TV show!; Can the other contestants survive Veronica's laziness?; Or will Betty teach the rich little princess how to rough it?; Either way, the ratings for this comic are sure to be through the roof!

"Cold Symptoms," Betty has a case of the winter doldrums, so to cheer her up Veronica throws a pool party at her indoor, heated pool.

"Sweet Treat!" one-page story, Archie doesn't let on to Veronica how much fun he's having at the ski lodge.

"Romance Throughout History," A humorous look at romance through the eras.

"Look Who's Not Talking!": Veronica gets her tonsils out and that means she can't talk for awhile. That's bad timing - she's about to debate Reggie in English class! When she decides to write everything out on a pad, however, she proves the pen is mightier than the boor!

"Prize Fooled": Veronica learns her talent really is shopping when she becomes a winning contestant on the game show, "Guess The Price!"

"And The Winner Is": Move over, Carson - Brigitte, Betty, and Veronica have just won a co-hosting spot on NTV's request video show!

Is Cheryl Blossom leaving Riverdale for good?! Don't miss this milestone issue!

"The Big Present": Yes, it's true: Cheryl Blossom - the girl who sets Archie's heart aflutter and puts Betty and Veronica up in arms - is leaving Riverdale! Of course, she's left before, only to return as the "spoiler" in the landmark "Love Showdown" storyline. But this time, it looks like she's going for good, as her father's business moves to Europe! Before she goes, she's inviting the whole Riverdale gang to her going-away party, and giving Betty and Veronica a most unexpected parting gift! It's an exit they'll always remember... and one you'll never forget!

"The Alternative Prom": Betty ponders holding an alternative prom - instead of pomp and circumstance, the students will entertain orphans instead! Of course, Veronica thinks it's a preposterous idea - until she realizes how much good publicity it could bring her if she were to propose it.

"Brigitte's On The Move" - Betty, Veronica and Frankie Valdez travel to Centerville to visit Brigitte. But when Betty & Veronica hear Frankie and Brigitte practicing sappy love songs in Brigitte's recording studio, they think Frankie is two-timing Maria! Wait till they find out who really has a crash on Brigitte!

"A Ride On The Wild Side": Veronica gets love-sick - literally, when her new date takes her on all the thrill rides at the amusement park!

"Mood For Thought": Betty and Veronica try out "moodkinis" - bikinis that change color with your moods!

Betty and Archie agree to staff Pop Tate's Hot Dog Cart at the local beach. Betty and Veronica decide to give Archie and Reggie a taste of their own medicine by making racy remarks about them as the boys pass.

"Friends 'Til the End!", Betty and Veronica's "perfect" friendship is put to the test when they win a "Best Friends in America" TV show contest; Unknown to each other, they've submitted very different definitions of friendship in their award-winning essays?; A fact the TV crew sent to film a typical day in their lives is all too aware of!; Can reality TV cancel Betty and Veronica's long-running friendship?

"Ginger Adds Spice," Betty and Veronica befriend new girl Ginger, but ask her to leave Archie to them. Ginger tricks them, and starts pursuing Archie herself.

"Action Faction" one-page story, The Riverdale cheerleaders are doing so well outshining the rival squad that they fail to notice how their football team is losing 40 to nothing.

"Make Room for Dilton," Who is the mysterious new love of Brigitte's life?; That's what Betty and Veronica aim to find out; And when they do, you won't believe the answer!; All is hearts and flowers, but not for long!; After all, this is an Archie comic, and cupid chaos reigns supreme as Archie spots Betty and Veronica giving Brigitte's beau romantic pointers!

"Up Close and Personal With Brigitte" character profile.

Lyrics to patriotic songs, in response to the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.

"Romance Throughout History" Part Two, The Archie characters are presented as historical figures from dinosaur days to the present, but always putting a romantic twist on historical events.

"This Girl's Everywhere," The girls scheme to keep Archie away from Ginger, but Jughead always tips her off in exchange for meals at the Lopez family's restaurant; Betty and Veronica neutralize him with an unlimited expense account at an all-you-can-eat buffet.

Notes:

  • The cover is a homage of the cover of Archie Annual #4.

"Cruisin' For Trouble": Looking for an escape from the winter doldrums, Betty and Veronica find themselves on a cruise to Alaska, courtesy of Brigitte who has a singing gig on the ship! It's smooth sailing until a crafty crooner tries to romance the girls and steal Brigitte's job. Oh, and did we mention that annoying iceberg?!

"It's About Time": Betty and Veronica take a wild trip through time, courtesy of Dilton's time machine! Along the way they encounter themselves at younger ages and even their parents before they were born! But when Veronica stays behind for a 1967 shopping spree, Dilton and Brigitte must help Betty rescue their friend from forever being lost to the ages! Of course, the time machine also goes forward, and when the girls find out Archie gets married, naturally they want to know who wound up being the bride... or do they?!

"Safari So Good": If you think Veronica leads a wild life now, wait till you see her exploits as a wildlife photographer in Africa! Her only mistake is packing a plush gorilla in her backpack. Now roughing it just got rougher, as a mother gorilla has claimed the stuffed animal... and Veronica... as her own!

"Psychic Shenanigans": Veronica hires a psychic to help her find a lost ring but before she's done, there may be lost greenbacks, too!

"Predictable Outcome": Betty is dressed for duress when she asks for Veronica's input on her new gown.

"Teen Spirit": Not all ghosts are scary - some are romantic! That's what Betty and Veronica learn when they explore an abandoned pirate ship... and are wooed by the teen ghost pirate who inhabits the crow's nest! But this ghost scares up trouble when he follows the girls back to Veronica's yacht and finds Archie, Reggie and Jughead there!

"The Mod Hatter," Ethel tries to attract attention by wearing different hats.

"Big Apple Daze," The girls show Ginger that she can feel more at home in Riverdale while not forgetting about her former home in New York City.

"Race Around the World," Betty and Veronica team up to enter a reality show contest where they must arrive at a predetermined destination first and under budget.

"Got a Lot of Homework?" Betty and Veronica's Study Tips article.

"Modern Pioneers," Once again, Veronica's idea of roughing it is using portable electronics.

"The Dream Team," Betty describes the many unguessed aspects of shopping with Veronica.

"Toy Story," Betty and Archie drag Veronica along to look over a recently opened toy store.

"Switching Places," In this spoof of the popular TV show, "Trading Spaces," Betty and Veronica are given two days each to redecorate each other's bedrooms!; But are they just out to makeover their rooms...or makeover each other, too?!; You don't need a TV to learn the answer—just pick up this colossal comic!

"New Dos for 2002" Betty and Veronica illustration.

"Too Many Friends?", Betty falls asleep while watching "Friends" and dreams she and her friends are part of the cast.

"Dream Demon," Reggie suffers for something Archie dreamed.

"Skate Checkmate," Veronica can't fathom why Betty gave up figure skating in favor of co-ed ice hockey.

By Popular Demand, "Archie's Angels" Return! in "The Return of Archie's Angels," Those glamorous, adventurous agents who made their smashing debut in Betty & Veronica #44 are back...and with Brigitte Reilly unavailable, they recruit a new third angel to join them in their derring-do: Ginger Lopez!; This time they're charged with rescuing kidnapped scientist Dilton Doiley Esquire III!; Who could have kidnapped him...and why?; The mission will take our heroines jet setting across the globe and tackling megalomaniacal madmen and roughhousing robots! Will the angels earn their wings...or will they end up playing harps?!

"Bizarre Bazaar," Betty and Veronica, along with Nancy, get up at four a.m. to be in line to purchase designer shoes at a fraction of their original cost from a charity event.

"How To Meet Boys," Betty and Veronica make an instructional DVD on how to meet boys.

"Princess and the Pauper," Betty and Veronica switch places; Veronica goes to visit Betty's relatives in the country while Betty goes to visit royalty in England.

"Chances Are..."; Betty and Veronica both use their position in the school office to change the schedule of a new exchange student.

"A Fowl Scent" Veronica Lodge, Jughead Jones, Jellybean Jones, Forsythe Jones, Gladys Jones, and Hiram Lodge.

Hot Roddin' in the "Fifties" Pals 'n' Gals illustration.

"A Vacation From Archie": Inspired by how well-rounded Ginger and Brigitte are, Betty and Veronica decide to expand their world by cutting back on Archie and taking up new hobbies... but everywhere they turn, Archie is there! Could it be he's a permanent fixture in their lives?!

"Surf's Up": Veronica can't compete with Ginger when it comes to riding the waves... until she climbs aboard Dilton's remote control surf board! "Diary of a Mad Teenager": When she catches Veronica peeking into her diary, Betty prepares a phony one filled with disparaging comments about her rich friend!

"Hail to the Chiefs": It's a homework assignment of presidential proportions when Ms. Grundy asks the class to write about how they'd run the country! Needless to say, Betty and Veronica have very different ideas on how to be a commander-in-chief! Can Betty's fair, benevolent platform compete with Veronica's decisive, forceful, and opinionated style? The White House will never be the same!

"Best in Show?": When Betty has to watch her aunt's cuter-than-cute dog, Veronica suffers from attention deficit! How can Veronica compete with a canine and regain her position as the center of attention? By getting her own dog, of course... a show dog at that!

It's an all-new look for Betty & Veronica Spectacular! Taking cues from women's and teen magazines, the series takes on fashion, relationship advice, the latest trends, and more! In addition to comic book stories covering these themes, readers can look forward to fresh features like personality quizzes, fashion pages, and more!

"Fashion Don'ts": Betty and Veronica decide the "burden" of fashion shouldn't rest entirely on girls' shoulders and give the boys of Riverdale High a makeover... but will the boys still be duds even in their new duds?

"Fairytale Fashion": Ginger asks Betty to help her come up with some new fashion ideas for her latest magazine article, and a fateful night of babysitting provides her with all the inspiration she needs!

"Prom Here to Eternity": It's a trip through fashion history in this story that highlights the century's prom fashions.

In order to counter the effects of Betty's supposed enchanted locket, Veronica goes to a phony fortune teller and gets a love talisman of her own guaranteed to win her Archie's undying affections. Betty wins a contest securing her and Veronica bit parts on their favorite television show. Betty invents a hair styling tool from a bent coat hanger.

Veronica wants company at the beach since all her friends have babysitting jobs. The girls decide to hire Myrtle, a lifeguard, so that they can all have fun at the beach, but Myrtle takes over, ordering the girls around and even chasing the boys away. The boys keep dumping buckets of water on the girls, so Veronica orders a shipment of snowballs from Alaska to fight back.

"Fashion 101": When Ms. Grundy admires a poncho of Betty's, the girls make one for her. Before you know it the girls are designing clothes for the whole faculty!

"Going Solo": What every band fears: two members of "The Archies" have decided to break off on their own and form an acoustic duo!

"What a Card": When Betty sends out a Christmas card featuring a cute photo of herself, it's a smash hit. So much so, that Veronica vows to outdo Betty, by creating a whole Christmas card calendar filled with Veronica photos!

"Band Together": It's the 30th anniversary of the rock band "Kickz," and one lucky Riverdale High teen is going to win a chance to take the stage and rock and roll all night with the legendary rockers! Wait until you see who wins (that is, if you can recognize them under their cool rockin' makeup)!

"Guitar-Mania": When she spots Brigitte and Betty with personalized guitars, Veronica has an "axe" to grind and gets one for herself!

"Give Me a Spring Break," Betty postpones a trip to the Bahamas with Veronica to head up a committee of kids spending their Spring Break beautifying the community; Veronica decides to help in order to speed things along...but once she gets a taste of landscaping fever, she may not want to leave!

"Prom Date Disasters"; Betty and Veronica reminisce about prom night disasters.

"Spring Gardening Tips"; Betty and Veronica give tips on how to garden.

"Spring Break Quiz"; Quiz about Springtime.

"Betty, Veronica, & Ginger's Prom Glitz!" fashion page; Betty, Veronica, and Ginger model their prom dresses.

75th Issue Anniversary Blow-Out! "Fashion Victims": Ginger comes up with the best Sparkle Magazine Fashion Show theme yet: "Are you a Betty or you a Veronica?" As one famous model after another sports the latest Betty-centric outfit or flashy Veronica couture, the hottest act in pop music, The Veronicas, provide the tuneful accompaniment!

"Jingle's Jangled!": Betty and Veronica are smitten by the new hunk at school. Just wait until they find out it's really Jingles, Santa's now ex-elf in disguise! Jingles hopes to get a taste of Archie's life, but soon realizes the snow isn't always whiter on the other side of the sleigh!

"Present Tense": When Betty and Veronica spot Archie picking up a giant self-portrait at the photo shop, each thinks it's their Christmas gift!

"The Great Outdoors: Betty Style!": Camping in the wilderness has its disadvantages for Veronica - namely, no malls, no electricity, and no plumbing. But before she can bail, Veronica spots hunky Donald on the trail, and suddenly, the lack of luxuries become irrelevant!

'The Great Outdoors: Veronica Style': In a flip of the previous story, Veronica hosts a camping trip, and no convenience is left behind! But even high energy power lines aren't infallible, so Betty may get her wish of 'roughing it' yet!

"High School Switcheroo," Wanting the students to try something different, the faculty switch the students' first period elective to something they're unfamiliar with; Veronica is enrolled in "Domestic Living" while Betty is signed up for "Corporate Business"; Both girls struggle in their assigned electives: Betty has to make hard business decisions including layoffs, presentations and mergers, while Veronica deals with carpentry, cooking and car engine repair.

"Homework the Easy Way!", The girls share their secrets for getting good grades in school.

"B&V's Time For A Change Quiz!", A quiz to determine if you like change or prefer things more stable. Back To School

"What Class Is Right For You?", The gang discovers which electives are best for them.

issue_title: Fitness Fiasco; Hold the Phone; Moody & Snooty
description: Betty and Veronica agree to try each others exercise regime for a week to see which one is better. A wrong number left on Betty's answering machine leads her to think she's stumbled onto a mob hit.

"Extreme Decorating," A contest for the 'most inspiring holiday display' inspires Veronica to break out all the bells and whistles...and lights...and ornaments...and tinsel...and you get the idea!; When compared to more tasteful displays, it looks like Veronica's over-the-top extravaganza may only inspire a high power bill...but little does Veronica suspect it could actually lead to a very personal holiday miracle, too!

"Holiday Gifts You Can Make Cheap!", The gang shows that they don't have to spend a lot of money to give a gift from the heart.

"B & V Holiday Style," Two pages of fan-designed fashions.

"Eco-Friendly Green Christmas Tips," Tips on how to have an environmentally-sound Christmas.

Led by Tomoko and her brother Akira, the kids at Riverdale High ask 'How Green Can You Go?' in a big way, by having an eco-friendly winter dance, but the only 'green' Veronica is willing to commit to is money!; Will she change her mind when her father offers to host the dance in the new solar-powered wing of his estate?; Or will it take one hunky enviro-boy to make her see the light?; Don't miss this exciting story loaded with off-the-grid environmental tips and off-the-chart laughs!

"B&V's How Green Are you Quiz?"; A scored quiz to determine how eco-friendly the reader is.

"Betty & Veronica's Guide To Green Dating," The gang explains how they conserve energy and resources.

In this special 'Love & Romance' issue, Betty and Veronica are shocked to find Archie attending a wedding - with Cheryl Blossom as his date! Things get even worse for Veronica when Betty gets upgraded to bridesmaid. 'For Better or Worse,' Veronica will find a way to take center stage at this event! Plus, take a peak into Betty and Veronica's romantic futures - according to them!

It's a special 'Summy Fun' issue with those teen scene dreams, Betty & Veronica! When both the boys and the girls claim the same exact spot in the cove as their exclusive place to hang out, 'The Battle For Riverdale Cove' is on! They hold a multi-game contest to determine who has dibs. When they get to the 'treasure hunt' portion of the competition, imagine their surprise when they stumble upon a bag of coins and jewels! Will the two teams put aside their rivalry long enough to team-up and solve this mystery?

When Veronica finds herself perpetually late for school, her father insists that she needs some 'Get Up & Go,' and she can begin by riding the bus! Will she give up the creature comforts of her father's limo so easily, or come up with an alternate way to travel with style?

Special Halloween Issue! It's a dark and stormy night, a fitting night for Betty and Veronica to stay inside and have a scary movie festival! But things go from 'reel' to real when Archie, Jughead, and Reggie try to crash the girls' private party - and come face-to-face with an axe-wielding maniac! Is everything as it seems, or is it just a case of the boys' imaginations running wild? Guest-starring Veronica's truck driving-aunt, Tessie!

Special holiday issue! The Sugar Plum fairy is convinced that Betty and Veronica are being manipulated by Archie; while Jingles the Elf thinks Archie would be better off without the girls. They each decide to take matters into their diminutive hands - by adopting human forms to distract the teens! Will their diversions dismantle the love triangle for good, or will there be a merry - and romantic - Christmas for everyone after all?

Betty and Veronica trade fashionable chic for intrepid mystique in this action-packed issue! In 'Where the Action Is!,' perhaps the most aptly-titled tale of the year, Betty and Veronica deliver high-octane action and adventure as the most super secret agents ever to tackle a viperous spy - not to mention the most beautiful! Equipped by Dilton with the latest high tech crime-fighting gadgets, the girls are on the case as Archie goes missing - and the usual suspects are quickly rounded up. But will the real suspect be someone a bit more unusual? You'll never guess! All this plus 'Action Fashions,' an action movie quiz, gadget pages and more!

Betty and Archie get jobs on the 'Geek Patrol,' a group of computer tech-sperts seen in last month's Veronica #193. To keep Betty from spending so much time with Archie, Veronica joins the squad, too - and it isn't long before she inadvertently unleashes a vicious computer virus! Co-starring computer gurus Dilton and Veronica's cousin, Marcy, this 'geek-tacular' issue also features a 'techie' quiz, internet tips, geek-chic fashions, and more!

Get set to wax up your board and ride the waves in this surf-tacular issue! When a reality show about a hunky surfer hits Riverdale, guess which rich girl is first in line to be an extra? Rainy days don't put a damper on Betty and Veronica's surfing - not when they can 'surf indoors' with their interactive 'Whee' gaming system! Plus, summer fun fashions and quizzes!

Veronica gives Archie a medallion with a GPS tracker embedded in it so she can keep track of him at all times. Betty is covering her cousin's paper route and Veronica offers to help. Inspired by the yard sale the Coopers conduct, the Lodges hold one as well.

It's a boy band brouhaha, as Betty and Veronica get jobs as reporters for Ginger Lopez's "Glitz Magazine" and have a controversial run-in with The Juneau Brothers! Then, to gossip or not to gossip, that is the rumor! Finally, Mr. Lodge reveals a sensational secret from his past: he once dated a celebrity! All this, plus pop-culture extras like a Hollywood quiz, celebrity fashions, and more!
